name: Cosine similarity
description: A score from -1 to 1 measuring how closely two vectors point the same way: the cosine of the angle between them.

name: Dot product
description: Multiplying two equal-length vectors entry by entry and summing the products, giving one number that reflects both their lengths and how aligned they are.

name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
description: An eigenvector of a square matrix is a nonzero vector the matrix merely scales without turning; the scaling factor is its eigenvalue.

name: Element-wise product
description: Multiplying two same-shaped vectors or matrices entry by entry, producing a result of the same shape.

name: Identity matrix
description: A square matrix with ones on its main diagonal and zeros elsewhere, which leaves any vector unchanged when multiplied by it.

name: Linear independence
description: A set of vectors is linearly independent when none of them can be built by scaling and adding the others.

name: Linear transformation
description: A function from vectors to vectors that preserves addition and scaling; multiplying a vector by a fixed matrix is exactly such a function.

name: Low-rank decomposition
description: Writing (or approximating) a large matrix as the product of two thin matrices, which stores far fewer numbers when its rank is low.

name: Matrix
description: A rectangular grid of numbers arranged in rows and columns, used to store data or to transform vectors.

name: Matrix inverse
description: The matrix that undoes a square matrix's effect, so multiplying the two gives the identity matrix; not every matrix has one.

name: Matrix multiplication
description: Combining two matrices so each entry of the result is the dot product of a row of the first with a column of the second.

name: Matrix norm
description: A single number measuring the overall size of a matrix, for example the square root of the sum of all its squared entries.

name: Matrix transpose
description: Flipping a matrix over its main diagonal so that its rows become columns and its columns become rows.

name: Orthogonality
description: Two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero, which geometrically means they meet at a right angle.

name: Outer product
description: Multiplying a column vector by a row vector to get a matrix holding every pairwise product of their entries.

name: Rank of a matrix
description: The largest number of linearly independent columns in a matrix, which always equals the largest number of linearly independent rows.

name: Rotation matrix
description: A square matrix that rotates vectors around the origin, preserving their lengths and the angles between them.

name: Scalar
description: A single number, like 3 or -0.5, used on its own rather than as part of a list or grid of numbers.

name: Singular value decomposition
description: Factoring any matrix into three simple steps: a rotation, a stretch along perpendicular axes, and another rotation; the stretch amounts are its singular values.

name: Subspace
description: A vector space sitting inside a larger one, such as a flat plane through the origin within ordinary 3-D space.

name: Tensor
description: In deep learning, a multidimensional grid of numbers that generalizes scalars (0-D), vectors (1-D), and matrices (2-D) to any number of dimensions.

name: Vector
description: An ordered list of numbers, which can be pictured as an arrow or a point in space.

name: Vector norm
description: A single number measuring a vector's length or size, such as its ordinary straight-line (Euclidean) length.

name: Vector space
description: A set of vectors in which adding any two, or scaling one by a number, always gives another vector in the set.

name: Argmax
description: The input at which a function takes its largest value: max gives that largest value, while argmax gives where it occurs.

name: Big-O notation
description: Notation for how fast a cost such as running time or memory grows with input size n, ignoring constant factors, as in O(n^2).

name: Chain rule
description: The rule for differentiating nested functions: the derivative of f(g(x)) is f's derivative at g(x) times g's derivative at x.

name: Convex function
description: A bowl-shaped function: the straight line between any two points on its graph never dips below the graph, so every local minimum is global.

name: Derivative
description: How fast a function's output changes as its input changes at a given point; geometrically, the slope of its graph there.

name: Exponential function
description: The function e^x, where e is about 2.718; it is always positive and grows ever faster as x increases.

name: Function
description: A rule that assigns exactly one output to each input, such as f(x) = 2x + 1.

name: Gradient
description: The vector of all partial derivatives of a function with many inputs; it points in the direction in which the function increases fastest.

name: Gradient descent
description: An algorithm that minimizes a function by repeatedly taking small steps in the direction opposite to its gradient, that is, downhill.

name: Hessian matrix
description: The square matrix of all second partial derivatives of a many-input function, describing how its gradient changes, that is, its local curvature.

name: Integral
description: The accumulated total of a function's values over a range, pictured as the area under its graph; a continuous version of a sum.

name: Jacobian matrix
description: The matrix of all partial derivatives of a function with several inputs and outputs; row i is the gradient of the i-th output.

name: Learning rate
description: The step size in gradient descent: a positive number that scales how far the parameters move against the gradient on each update.

name: Local minimum
description: A point where a function is no higher than at any nearby point, though not necessarily the lowest overall (the global minimum).

name: Logarithm
description: The inverse of exponentiation: the logarithm base b of x answers 'b to what power equals x?', so log_2(8) = 3.

name: Mini-batch
description: A small random subset of training examples, such as 32 or 256, used to estimate the gradient for one stochastic gradient descent step.

name: Natural gradient descent
description: Gradient descent that measures step size by how much the model's predicted distribution changes, using Fisher information, rather than by raw parameter distance.

name: Newton's method
description: An optimizer that uses the Hessian's curvature as well as the gradient to choose each step, needing fewer but costlier steps than gradient descent.

name: Online convex optimization
description: A framework where, each round, a learner commits to a choice and then pays a convex loss that is revealed only afterward.

name: Partial derivative
description: The derivative of a function of several inputs with respect to one of them, holding all the other inputs fixed.

name: Polyak averaging
description: Averaging the parameter values visited over many training steps, instead of keeping only the last ones, to smooth out the noise of stochastic updates.

name: Regret bound
description: An upper limit on regret, the extra loss an online learner suffers compared with the best fixed choice in hindsight, e.g., O(sqrt(T)) over T rounds.

name: Saddle point
description: A point where the gradient is zero yet the function curves up in some directions and down in others, like the middle of a saddle.

name: Stochastic gradient descent
description: Gradient descent that estimates the gradient from a few randomly chosen training examples at each step, making updates cheap but noisy.

name: Summation notation
description: Using the Greek letter sigma (Σ) as shorthand for adding up a series of terms, like x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_n.

name: Taylor series
description: Writing a function near a point as a sum of terms built from its derivatives there; keeping the first few terms gives a simple approximation.

name: Trigonometric functions
description: Functions such as sine and cosine that relate an angle to coordinates on a circle; their values repeat as the angle keeps increasing.

name: Bayes' rule
description: A formula for reversing a conditional probability: P(A | B) equals P(B | A) times P(A), divided by P(B).

name: Bernoulli distribution
description: The distribution of a single yes/no trial that gives 1 with probability p and 0 otherwise, like one flip of a possibly biased coin.

name: Bias of an estimator
description: The difference between the expected value of an estimate computed from random data and the true quantity it estimates; an unbiased estimate has zero.

name: Categorical distribution
description: The distribution of a single trial with K possible outcomes, each with its own probability, like one roll of a possibly loaded die.

name: Conditional probability
description: The probability that one event happens given that another event is known to have happened, written P(A | B).

name: Covariance
description: A measure of how two random variables vary together: positive when they tend to rise together, negative when one rises as the other falls.

name: Covariance matrix
description: A square matrix holding the covariance between every pair of variables in a set, with each variable's own variance on the diagonal.

name: Entropy
description: The average uncertainty of a random outcome: the minimum expected number of bits needed to describe a draw from its distribution.

name: Expectation
description: The probability-weighted average of a random variable's possible values, matching the long-run average over many repeated draws.

name: Exponential moving average
description: A running average updated with each new value, weighting recent values most while older values' influence shrinks by a constant factor each step.

name: Fisher information
description: How much observed data reveal about a model's parameters, defined as the variance (covariance matrix, for many parameters) of the log-likelihood's gradient.

name: Importance sampling
description: Estimating an expectation under one distribution using samples drawn from another, weighting each sample by the ratio of the two distributions' probabilities.

name: Independent and identically distributed
description: Describes a collection of random samples that are all drawn from the same distribution, with no sample influencing any other.

name: Joint distribution
description: The probability distribution of two or more random variables together, giving how likely each combination of their values is.

name: KL divergence
description: A non-symmetric measure of how one probability distribution differs from another: the expected extra bits paid for encoding data with the wrong distribution.

name: Likelihood
description: How probable the observed data are under a model, viewed as a function of the model's parameters with the data held fixed.

name: Marginal distribution
description: The distribution of one variable on its own, obtained from a joint distribution by summing (or integrating) over the other variables.

name: Markov chain
description: A random process moving between states where the chance of each next state depends only on the current state, not on earlier history.

name: Maximum likelihood estimation
description: Choosing the parameter values that make the observed data most probable, that is, the values that maximize the likelihood.

name: Mean
description: The average of a set of numbers: add them all up and divide by how many there are.

name: Moments of a distribution
description: Expected values of powers of a random variable, E[X^k]; the first moment is the mean, and the second moment about the mean is the variance.

name: Monte Carlo estimation
description: Approximating an expected value by averaging a quantity over many random samples, with the error shrinking as the number of samples grows.

name: Normal distribution
description: The bell-shaped continuous distribution, set by its mean and standard deviation, that many natural quantities and sums of random effects approximately follow.

name: Partition function
description: The normalizing constant that divides unnormalized scores so they sum, or integrate, to one, turning them into a valid probability distribution.

name: Posterior distribution
description: The updated probability distribution over an unknown quantity after seeing data, found by combining the prior with the likelihood via Bayes' rule.

name: Prior distribution
description: A probability distribution expressing what you believe about an unknown quantity before seeing any data.

name: Probability
description: A number from 0 to 1 expressing how likely an event is, where 0 means impossible and 1 means certain.

name: Probability density function
description: For a continuous random variable, a curve whose area over any range of values gives the probability of landing in that range.

name: Probability distribution
description: A description of how likely each possible value of a random variable is, such as a fair die giving each face probability 1/6.

name: Random variable
description: A quantity whose value depends on the outcome of a random process, such as the number shown by a rolled die.

name: Standard deviation
description: The square root of the variance, measuring the typical spread of values around the mean in the same units as the data.

name: Standardization
description: Rescaling a variable by subtracting its mean and dividing by its standard deviation, giving it mean 0 and standard deviation 1.

name: Statistical independence
description: Two random variables are independent when knowing one tells nothing about the other, so their joint probability is the product of their separate probabilities.

name: Variance
description: The expected squared distance of a random variable from its mean, measuring how spread out its values are.

name: Whitening
description: Transforming data so its features have variance 1 and zero covariance with each other, usually using the eigenvectors of its covariance matrix.

name: Bias-variance tradeoff
description: The balance between models too simple to capture the pattern (high bias) and models so flexible they fit noise (high variance).

name: Classification
description: A prediction task where the model assigns each input to one of a fixed set of categories, like spam or not spam.

name: Contrastive learning
description: Learning embeddings by pulling together pairs that belong together, like two crops of one photo, and pushing apart pairs that don't.

name: Covariate shift
description: When the inputs a model sees after deployment are distributed differently from its training inputs, while the input-to-label relationship stays the same.

name: Cross-entropy loss
description: A classification loss equal to the negative log of the probability the model gave the correct class, so confident mistakes cost the most.

name: Ensemble learning
description: Combining predictions from several separately trained models, by voting or averaging, to get more accurate and reliable results than any single one.

name: Feature
description: One measurable property of an example, such as a pixel's brightness or a word count, that a model uses as input.

name: Few-shot learning
description: Learning a new class or task from only a handful of labeled examples, usually by building on knowledge from earlier training.

name: Generalization
description: How well a model performs on new examples it never saw during training, which is the real goal of learning.

name: Hyperparameter
description: A setting chosen before training, such as how fast to learn or how big the model is, rather than learned from data.

name: Inductive bias
description: The built-in assumptions that make a learning method prefer some solutions over others, like a vision model assuming nearby pixels are related.

name: L2 regularization
description: Adding the sum of squared weights to the loss, pushing training toward smaller weights and smoother models that overfit less.

name: Label
description: The correct answer attached to a training example, such as 'cat' for a photo, which a model learns to predict.

name: Linear regression
description: Predicting a number as a weighted sum of the input features plus a constant, with weights chosen to minimize mean squared error.

name: Logistic regression
description: A classification model that feeds a weighted sum of features through the sigmoid function to output the probability of the positive class.

name: Logits
description: The raw scores a classifier outputs for each class before softmax turns them into probabilities; a higher score means more likely.

name: Loss function
description: A formula that scores how wrong a model's predictions are; training adjusts the parameters to make this score as small as possible.

name: Machine learning
description: Getting computers to learn patterns from example data so they improve at a task, rather than following hand-written rules.

name: Mean squared error
description: A loss that averages the squared differences between predicted and true numbers, so large mistakes are punished much more than small ones.

name: Model parameters
description: The numbers inside a model, such as weights and biases, that training adjusts so the model's predictions fit the data.

name: One-hot encoding
description: Representing one of K categories as a vector of K zeros with a single 1 at that category's position.

name: Overfitting
description: When a model fits its training data so closely, noise included, that it performs much worse on new data.

name: Principal component analysis
description: A method that finds the directions along which data varies most and keeps only the top few, compressing data while losing little information.

name: Regression
description: A prediction task where the model outputs a continuous number, such as a house price or tomorrow's temperature, rather than a category.

name: Regularization
description: Any technique that discourages a model from becoming overly complex, so it fits training data less tightly and generalizes better.

name: Self-supervised learning
description: Learning from unlabeled data by making the labels from the data itself, such as hiding part of an input and predicting it.

name: Sigmoid function
description: An S-shaped function, 1/(1+e^-x), that squashes any number into the range 0 to 1 so it can be read as a probability.

name: Softmax
description: A function that turns a list of scores into probabilities that are positive and sum to one, giving the largest score the biggest share.

name: Softmax temperature
description: A number that divides the scores before softmax: high values make the probabilities more equal, low values concentrate them on the top choice.

name: Supervised learning
description: Learning from examples that each come with the correct answer, so the model learns to map new inputs to the right outputs.

name: Train/validation/test split
description: Dividing data into a training set to fit the model, a validation set to tune choices, and a test set for a final honest score.

name: Unsupervised learning
description: Finding structure, such as groups of similar items or a simpler summary, in data that comes without any correct-answer labels.

name: Zero-shot learning
description: Handling classes or tasks a model never saw labeled examples of during training, using descriptions or general knowledge instead.

name: Activation function
description: The nonlinear function a neuron applies to its weighted sum; without it, stacked layers could only represent straight-line relationships.

name: AdaGrad
description: An adaptive optimizer that divides each parameter's step by the root of its summed squared past gradients, so frequently updated parameters slow down.

name: Adam optimizer
description: A widely used optimizer that combines momentum with per-parameter step sizes scaled by recent squared gradients, working well with little tuning.

name: AdaMax
description: A variant of Adam that scales steps by the largest recent gradient magnitude, the infinity norm, instead of an average of squared gradients.

name: AdamW
description: A version of Adam that applies weight decay directly to the weights, separate from the gradient-based step, making regularization work as intended.

name: Adaptive learning rate
description: Optimizers that automatically give each parameter its own step size, based on the history of that parameter's gradients.

name: Artificial neuron
description: A simple computing unit that takes a weighted sum of its inputs, adds a bias, and passes the result through a nonlinear function.

name: Automatic differentiation
description: Software that computes exact derivatives of a program by recording its basic operations and applying the chain rule to them automatically.

name: Backpropagation
description: The algorithm that computes how each weight affects the loss by applying the chain rule backward through the network, layer by layer.

name: Batch normalization
description: Standardizing each layer's inputs using the mean and variance of the current mini-batch, then applying a learned scale and shift.

name: Bias correction
description: Adam's rescaling of its running averages early in training, since averages that start at zero would otherwise be biased toward zero.

name: Classification head
description: The final layer or layers that turn a network's learned features into one score per class, usually followed by softmax.

name: Cosine learning rate decay
description: A schedule that lowers the learning rate along a cosine curve, from its starting value smoothly down to near zero.

name: Deep learning
description: Machine learning with neural networks that have many layers, which learn useful features directly from raw data like pixels or text.

name: Distributed training
description: Splitting the work of training one model across many processors or machines, by dividing up the data, the model, or both.

name: Downstream task
description: The specific task you actually care about, such as spam detection, that a pretrained model is adapted to.

name: Dropout
description: Randomly switching off a fraction of neurons at each training step, so the network can't rely on any single one and overfits less.

name: Early stopping
description: Stopping training when performance on the validation set stops improving, before the model starts to overfit.

name: Embedding
description: A learned vector of numbers that represents an item, like a word or an image, so similar items get nearby vectors.

name: Epoch
description: One complete pass through every example in the training set; training usually runs for many epochs.

name: Exploding gradient problem
description: When gradients grow at every layer during backpropagation, becoming so large that training updates turn wildly unstable.

name: Fine-tuning
description: Continuing to train a pretrained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset so it adapts to that task.

name: Forward pass
description: Feeding an input through a network layer by layer to compute its output and, during training, the loss.

name: Fully connected layer
description: A layer where every output neuron is connected to every input with its own weight, computed as a matrix multiplication plus a bias.

name: GELU
description: A smooth, ReLU-like activation that multiplies each input by the chance that a standard normal value falls below it.

name: Gradient clipping
description: Shrinking gradients whose size exceeds a set limit before each update, so one huge gradient can't derail training.

name: Group normalization
description: Standardizing each example's values within groups of feature maps, which works well even with the tiny batches where batch norm struggles.

name: He initialization
description: Setting starting weights randomly with variance 2 divided by the number of inputs, so signal sizes stay steady through ReLU layers.

name: Hidden layer
description: A layer of neurons between a network's input and output, whose values are intermediate features the network learns on its own.

name: Internal covariate shift
description: The way the inputs to a deep layer keep changing distribution during training, because the layers before it keep updating.

name: Knowledge distillation
description: Training a small student model to match the output probabilities of a large teacher model, transferring much of its skill cheaply.

name: Label smoothing
description: Training against softened targets, like 0.9 for the correct class with the remaining 0.1 spread over others, so the model is less overconfident.

name: Layer normalization
description: Standardizing each example's activations across a layer's features, using that example's own mean and variance, then applying a learned scale and shift.

name: Learning rate schedule
description: A plan for changing the learning rate during training, typically lowering it over time so training settles into a good solution.

name: Learning rate warmup
description: Starting training with a tiny learning rate and gradually raising it over the first steps, which prevents unstable early updates.

name: Mini-batch statistics
description: The mean and variance of the current mini-batch, which batch norm uses during training, switching to running averages at test time.

name: Momentum
description: An optimizer technique that keeps a running average of past gradients and steps along it, smoothing noisy updates and speeding progress.

name: Multilayer perceptron
description: The basic neural network: fully connected layers stacked one after another with a nonlinear activation between them.

name: Neural network
description: A model made of many artificial neurons arranged in layers, where each layer's outputs become the next layer's inputs.

name: Overparameterization
description: Using a model with far more parameters than training examples, which in deep learning surprisingly often still generalizes well.

name: Pretraining
description: Training a model first on a large, general dataset so it learns broadly useful features before being adapted to specific tasks.

name: Quantization
description: Storing a model's numbers with fewer bits, like 8-bit integers instead of 32-bit decimals, to make it smaller and faster.

name: ReLU
description: An activation function that passes positive inputs through unchanged and turns negative inputs into zero; the default in most deep networks.

name: Residual connection
description: A shortcut that adds a block's input to its output, so signals and gradients flow easily through very deep networks.

name: RMSNorm
description: A simpler layer normalization that only divides values by their root mean square, skipping mean subtraction; common in modern language models.

name: RMSProp
description: An adaptive optimizer that divides each step by a running average of recent squared gradients, so step sizes don't shrink forever like AdaGrad's.

name: Saturating nonlinearities
description: Activation functions like sigmoid and tanh that flatten out for large inputs, where their derivative is nearly zero and learning stalls.

name: Tanh
description: An S-shaped activation function that maps any number into the range -1 to 1, a zero-centered, stretched version of the sigmoid.

name: Transfer learning
description: Reusing what a model learned on one task or dataset to get a head start on a different but related task.

name: Vanishing gradient problem
description: When gradients shrink a little at every layer during backpropagation, so in deep networks the early layers get almost no learning signal.

name: Weight decay
description: Shrinking every weight slightly toward zero at each training step, which keeps weights small and reduces overfitting.

name: Weight freezing
description: Keeping some of a model's weights fixed during training, usually the pretrained layers, so only the remaining parts are updated.

name: Weight initialization
description: How a network's weights are set before training starts; poor choices make signals and gradients vanish or explode.

name: Xavier initialization
description: Setting starting weights randomly with variance based on a layer's number of inputs and outputs, so signal sizes stay steady across layers.

name: 1x1 convolution
description: A convolution whose kernel covers a single pixel, mixing information across feature maps at each position, often to cheaply change their number.

name: AlexNet
description: The 2012 convolutional neural network whose large win in the ImageNet challenge, using ReLU and dropout, launched the deep learning boom.

name: Bottleneck block
description: A residual block that shrinks the number of feature maps with a 1x1 convolution, applies a 3x3 convolution, then expands them back, saving computation.

name: CLIP
description: A model trained on image-caption pairs to place matching images and texts close together in a shared embedding space, enabling zero-shot image classification.

name: Convolution
description: Sliding a small grid of weights, called a kernel, across an input and computing a dot product with each patch it covers.

name: Convolutional layer
description: A neural network layer that applies many learned kernels to its input by convolution, producing one feature map per kernel.

name: Convolutional neural network
description: A neural network built mainly from convolutional and pooling layers, designed to learn patterns in grid-like data such as images.

name: Data augmentation
description: Creating extra training examples by applying label-preserving changes, such as flips, crops, or color shifts, to existing data.

name: Degradation problem
description: The finding that stacking more layers onto a deep network without shortcuts can increase its training error, so overfitting cannot be the cause.

name: Digital image
description: A picture stored as a grid of pixels, each holding numbers for brightness or for color channels such as red, green, and blue.

name: Feature map
description: The grid of outputs produced by applying one convolutional kernel across an input, showing where its pattern appears.

name: Global average pooling
description: Averaging each entire feature map down to a single number, turning a network's final feature maps into one vector.

name: GoogLeNet
description: A 22-layer convolutional network from 2014 built from Inception modules, which run several kernel sizes in parallel and concatenate the results.

name: Identity shortcut
description: A shortcut in a residual block that copies the input unchanged to the block's output, adding no extra parameters.

name: Image classification
description: The task of assigning a whole image one label from a fixed set of categories, such as cat, dog, or car.

name: Object detection
description: The task of finding every object of interest in an image, drawing a box around each, and labeling its category.

name: Patch embedding
description: Cutting an image into small square patches and mapping each to a vector with a learned linear transformation, making the image a token sequence.

name: Pooling layer
description: A layer that shrinks a feature map by summarizing each small window, typically with its maximum or average value.

name: Projection shortcut
description: A residual shortcut that passes the input through a learned 1x1 convolution so its shape matches the block's output when sizes change.

name: Receptive field
description: The region of the original input image that can influence a particular unit in a convolutional network's feature map.

name: Residual block
description: A few layers whose output is added back to their own input, so they only need to learn a change, or residual.

name: Residual network
description: A very deep convolutional network built from residual blocks, whose shortcut connections let networks with over a hundred layers train well.

name: Semantic segmentation
description: The task of labeling every pixel in an image with the category it belongs to, such as road, person, or sky.

name: Translation equivariance
description: The property that shifting an input image shifts a convolution's output by the same amount, so a pattern is detected wherever it appears.

name: U-Net
description: A U-shaped convolutional network that shrinks feature maps to capture context, then enlarges them back, copying fine detail across to produce per-pixel outputs.

name: VGG network
description: A deep convolutional network from Oxford's Visual Geometry Group built by stacking many small 3x3 convolutional layers, showing that depth improves accuracy.

name: Vision Transformer
description: A transformer for images that splits a picture into fixed-size patches and processes them like a sequence of word tokens.

name: Autoregressive model
description: A model that generates a sequence one element at a time, predicting each element from all the elements it has produced so far.

name: Beam search
description: A decoding method that keeps the k most probable partial sequences at every step, rather than just one, to find a more probable overall output.

name: Bidirectional RNN
description: Two recurrent networks reading a sequence in opposite directions, so each position's representation reflects the words both before and after it.

name: BM25
description: A classic search-ranking formula that scores documents by how often they contain the query's words, favoring rare words and adjusting for document length.

name: Byte-pair encoding
description: A subword tokenization method that starts from single characters or bytes and repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent pair into a new token.

name: Constituency parsing
description: Breaking a sentence into a tree of nested phrases, such as noun phrases and verb phrases, that shows its grammatical structure.

name: Contextual word embeddings
description: Word vectors that depend on the surrounding sentence, so 'bank' gets different vectors in 'river bank' and 'bank loan'.

name: Dense retrieval
description: Finding relevant documents by turning the query and each document into embedding vectors and returning the documents whose vectors are most similar to the query's.

name: Encoder-decoder architecture
description: A network design in which an encoder turns the input into an internal representation and a decoder turns that representation into the output.

name: Gated recurrent unit
description: A simpler relative of the LSTM that uses two gates and no separate memory cell, often working about as well with fewer parameters.

name: Greedy decoding
description: Generating text by always choosing the single most likely next token at each step; fast, but it can miss better overall sequences.

name: Language model
description: A model that assigns probabilities to sequences of tokens, usually by predicting how likely each possible next token is given the ones before it.

name: Long-range dependencies
description: Links between elements far apart in a sequence, like a pronoun and a noun many words earlier, which recurrent networks struggle to capture.

name: Long short-term memory
description: A recurrent neural network whose cells use learned gates to decide what to store, forget, and output, so it can remember information over long sequences.

name: Machine translation
description: Automatically translating text from one human language into another, such as English into German.

name: N-gram
description: A run of n consecutive tokens in a text, such as the 2-gram 'New York'; counting them underlies early language models and metrics like BLEU.

name: Named entity recognition
description: Finding the names of things in text, such as people, organizations, places, and dates, and labeling each with its category.

name: Natural language inference
description: Deciding whether a hypothesis sentence follows from, contradicts, or is neutral toward a premise sentence.

name: Natural language processing
description: The field of building computer systems, today mostly machine-learning models, that understand, analyze, or generate human language such as English text.

name: Next-token prediction
description: Training a model to guess the next token of a text from all the tokens before it, the self-supervised objective behind GPT-style language models.

name: Nucleus sampling
description: Sampling each next token from the smallest set of most likely candidates whose probabilities add up to at least a threshold p, such as 0.9.

name: Question answering
description: The task of automatically answering questions asked in natural language, often by finding the answer within a given passage or document collection.

name: Recurrent neural network
description: A neural network that reads a sequence one step at a time, updating a hidden state that carries information forward from earlier steps.

name: Sentiment analysis
description: Classifying the opinion or feeling expressed in text, such as whether a product review is positive or negative.

name: Sequence-to-sequence model
description: A model that reads an input sequence, such as a sentence, and generates an output sequence of possibly different length, such as its translation.

name: State space model
description: A sequence model that carries a hidden state forward through learned linear update rules, letting it process very long sequences efficiently.

name: Subword tokenization
description: Tokenization that splits rare words into frequent pieces, such as 'tokenization' into 'token' and 'ization', so a fixed vocabulary can represent any word.

name: Teacher forcing
description: Training a sequence generator by feeding it the correct previous tokens, instead of its own earlier guesses, when it predicts each next token.

name: Text summarization
description: Automatically producing a shorter version of a text that keeps its most important information.

name: Tokenization
description: Splitting raw text into a sequence of small units called tokens, such as words, word pieces, or characters, that a model can process.

name: Top-k sampling
description: Generating text by randomly sampling each next token from only the k most likely candidates, adding variety while avoiding very unlikely words.

name: Weight tying
description: Using the same matrix for a language model's input word embeddings and its output layer that scores next tokens, saving parameters and often improving quality.

name: Word embedding
description: A learned vector for each word in a vocabulary, placed so that words used in similar contexts, like 'cat' and 'dog', get nearby vectors.

name: WordPiece
description: The subword tokenization method used by BERT, which builds its vocabulary by merging the symbol pairs that most increase the likelihood of the training text.

name: Additive attention
description: An attention method that scores how well a query matches a key with a small feed-forward network, first used in neural machine translation.

name: Attention mechanism
description: Letting a model focus on the most relevant parts of its input by averaging them with weights from a softmax over relevance scores.

name: BERT
description: Google's encoder-only transformer, pretrained by predicting hidden words from context on both sides, then fine-tuned for tasks like classification and question answering.

name: Causal masking
description: Blocking each position in attention from seeing later positions, so a model learning to predict the next token cannot peek at it.

name: Class token
description: A special learned token added at the start of the input whose final vector summarizes the whole sequence for classification, as in BERT.

name: Context window
description: The maximum number of tokens a model can take in and attend to at once; anything beyond it is invisible to the model.

name: Cross-attention
description: Attention where queries come from one sequence while keys and values come from another, letting, for example, a decoder look at the encoder's output.

name: Decoder-only transformer
description: A transformer in which each token attends only to earlier tokens, used to generate text one token at a time, as GPT does.

name: Encoder-only transformer
description: A transformer that keeps only the encoder stack, letting every token see the whole input, to build representations for understanding tasks rather than generating text.

name: Flash attention
description: Computing exact attention block by block in fast on-chip memory, never storing the full score matrix, so it runs faster and uses far less memory.

name: Gated linear unit
description: A layer multiplying two linear transformations of its input element by element, one first passed through a sigmoid-like function so it acts as a gate.

name: GPT
description: OpenAI's family of decoder-only transformer language models, pretrained to predict the next token on vast amounts of text; GPT stands for Generative Pretrained Transformer.

name: Grouped-query attention
description: Attention in which groups of query heads share one key and value head, shrinking the KV cache; with a single group it is multi-query attention.

name: KV cache
description: Storing the keys and values already computed for earlier tokens during generation, so each new token reuses them instead of recomputing the whole sequence.

name: Learned positional embedding
description: Position information stored as a trainable vector for each position, learned along with the rest of the model, as in BERT and GPT.

name: Masked language modeling
description: A training task where random tokens in a text are hidden and the model learns to predict them from the words on both sides.

name: Multi-head attention
description: Running several attention operations in parallel, each with its own learned weights, and combining their outputs so the model captures different relationships at once.

name: Next sentence prediction
description: A BERT pretraining task: given two sentences, predict whether the second actually followed the first in the original text or was picked at random.

name: Position-wise feed-forward network
description: The small two-layer network inside each transformer block, applied separately and identically to every token's vector after attention.

name: Positional encoding
description: Information about each token's position added to its embedding, because self-attention by itself ignores word order.

name: Pre-layer normalization
description: Placing layer normalization at the start of each transformer sublayer, inside the residual branch, which makes deep transformers train more stably than the original arrangement.

name: Quadratic complexity of attention
description: Self-attention compares every token with every other token, so its compute and memory grow with the square of the sequence length.

name: Queries, keys, and values
description: Three vectors that attention computes from its inputs: each query is compared with every key to decide how much of that key's value to take.

name: Residual dropout
description: Applying dropout to each transformer sublayer's output just before it is added back through the residual connection, to reduce overfitting.

name: Rotary position embedding
description: Encoding position by rotating each query and key vector by angles proportional to its position, so attention scores depend on how far apart tokens are.

name: Scaled dot-product attention
description: Attention that weights values by the softmax of query-key dot products, each divided by the square root of the key dimension to keep scores moderate.

name: Segment embedding
description: A learned vector added to each token's embedding to mark which of two input sentences it belongs to, so the model can tell them apart.

name: Self-attention
description: Attention where queries, keys, and values all come from the same sequence, so every token can draw information from every other token.

name: Sinusoidal positional encoding
description: Fixed position signals built from sine and cosine waves of different frequencies, added to token embeddings in the original transformer.

name: T5
description: Google's encoder-decoder transformer that frames every language task as turning input text into output text, pretrained by filling in masked spans.

name: Transformer
description: A neural network architecture built from stacked self-attention and feed-forward layers that processes all tokens in parallel; the basis of BERT and GPT.

name: Adapter layers
description: Small bottleneck networks inserted between the frozen layers of a pretrained transformer and trained alone to adapt the model to a new task.

name: Best-of-n sampling
description: Generating n candidate responses, scoring each with a reward model, and keeping the highest-scoring one, improving outputs without any further training.

name: Bradley-Terry model
description: A model of pairwise comparisons in which the probability that one option beats another is the sigmoid of the difference between their scores.

name: Chain-of-thought prompting
description: Prompting a language model to write out intermediate reasoning steps before its final answer, which often improves accuracy on multi-step problems.

name: Direct preference optimization
description: Training a language model directly on preference pairs with a simple classification-style loss, matching RLHF's goal without a separate reward model or reinforcement learning.

name: Hallucination
description: When a language model confidently produces content that sounds plausible but is false or unsupported by its sources, such as an invented citation.

name: Human preference data
description: Records of people comparing two or more model responses to the same prompt and marking which they prefer, used to train models toward human tastes.

name: Implicit reward model
description: The reward a DPO-trained model defines implicitly: how much more likely it makes a response than the reference model does, on a log scale.

name: In-context learning
description: A language model's ability to pick up a new task from a few examples written in its prompt, with no change to its weights.

name: Instruction tuning
description: Fine-tuning a language model on many tasks written as plain-language instructions with answers, so it learns to follow new instructions it has never seen.

name: Intrinsic dimension
description: The dimension of the smallest random subspace of a model's weights in which training still nearly matches full training; often surprisingly small for fine-tuning.

name: KL penalty
description: A term that lowers the reward in proportion to the KL divergence between the trained model and a reference model, discouraging large drifts.

name: Language model alignment
description: Steering a language model so its behavior matches what people intend and value, such as being helpful, honest, and harmless, rather than merely predicting text.

name: Large language model
description: A language model, usually a transformer with billions of parameters, pretrained on vast amounts of text so it can handle many language tasks.

name: Low-rank adaptation
description: Fine-tuning by freezing the original weights and learning a small low-rank update, the product of two thin matrices, added to selected weight matrices.

name: Mixture of experts
description: A layer of many expert subnetworks plus a router that sends each token to just a few, adding parameters without adding much computation.

name: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning
description: Adapting a large pretrained model to a new task by training only a small number of added or selected parameters while keeping the rest frozen.

name: Plackett-Luce model
description: A probability model for full rankings: choose the top item by a softmax over scores, then the next among those remaining, and so on.

name: Prefix tuning
description: Learning a short sequence of trainable vectors, placed before the input at every layer, that steers a frozen language model like a learned prompt.

name: Prompting
description: Getting a language model to do a task by writing instructions, questions, or examples as its input text, without changing its weights.

name: QLoRA
description: LoRA fine-tuning on top of a base model whose frozen weights are stored in 4-bit precision, so very large models fit on modest hardware.

name: Reference model
description: A frozen copy of the model from before preference training, kept as an anchor so the trained model does not drift too far from it.

name: Reinforcement learning from human feedback
description: Fine-tuning a language model with reinforcement learning to maximize scores from a reward model trained to predict which responses people prefer.

name: Retrieval-augmented generation
description: Having a language model answer using documents fetched by a search step and inserted into its prompt, so answers can draw on up-to-date, citable sources.

name: Reward hacking
description: When a model trained to maximize a reward exploits flaws in it, such as quirks a reward model overrates, scoring highly without truly behaving better.

name: Reward model
description: A model trained on human preference data to score how good a response is, standing in for human judgment during reinforcement learning.

name: Scaling laws
description: Empirical rules showing that a model's loss falls along a predictable straight line on log-log axes as its size, data, and compute grow.

name: Supervised fine-tuning
description: Further training a pretrained language model on example prompts paired with ideal responses, so it learns to respond in the desired way.

name: Autoencoder
description: A neural network trained to reconstruct its own input after squeezing it through a narrow middle layer, learning a compact code.

name: Classifier-free guidance
description: Steering a diffusion model toward a condition like a text prompt by amplifying the gap between its conditioned and unconditioned predictions.

name: Denoising autoencoder
description: An autoencoder trained to recover the original clean input from a deliberately corrupted, noisy copy, which forces it to learn robust features.

name: Diffusion model
description: A generative model that learns to reverse a gradual noising process, turning pure random noise into a realistic sample step by step.

name: Evidence lower bound
description: A computable lower bound on the log-likelihood of the data, maximized in place of the exact value, which is too hard to compute.

name: Generative adversarial network
description: A generative model in which a generator network makes fake samples and a discriminator network tries to spot them, each improving by competing.

name: Generative model
description: A model that learns the probability distribution of its training data so it can produce new, realistic samples resembling that data.

name: Latent diffusion model
description: A diffusion model that runs its denoising process in the compact latent space of a pretrained autoencoder rather than on raw pixels, cutting computation.

name: Latent space
description: A space of compact learned vectors where each point stands for a possible data example, and nearby points stand for similar examples.

name: Normalizing flow
description: A generative model that turns simple random noise into data through a chain of invertible transformations, so the exact likelihood can be computed.

name: Reparameterization trick
description: Rewriting a random sample as a fixed function of the model's parameters plus independent noise, so gradients can flow through the sampling step.

name: Variational autoencoder
description: An autoencoder that encodes each input as a probability distribution in latent space, so sampling from that space generates new data.

name: Variational inference
description: Approximating a hard-to-compute probability distribution, usually a posterior, by optimizing a simpler distribution to be as close to it as possible.

name: Actor-critic
description: A method pairing a policy network (the actor) that picks actions with a value network (the critic) that scores them to guide policy updates.

name: Advantage function
description: How much better taking a specific action in a state is than the policy's average behavior there: its Q-value minus the state's value.

name: Bellman equation
description: A recursive relationship saying a state's value equals the expected sum of the immediate reward and the discounted value of the next state.

name: Contextual bandit
description: A bandit problem where the agent sees features describing the situation before each choice, so the best option depends on that context.

name: Deep Q-network
description: Q-learning with a deep neural network estimating action values, stabilized by replaying stored past experience and a slowly updated copy of the network.

name: Discounted return
description: The sum of rewards from a given time onward, each multiplied by a discount factor between 0 and 1 once per step of delay.

name: Exploration-exploitation tradeoff
description: The dilemma between trying unfamiliar actions to learn more and choosing the action currently believed best to collect reward now.

name: Markov decision process
description: A formal description of a decision problem by states, actions, rewards, and transition probabilities, where outcomes depend only on the current state and action.

name: Multi-armed bandit
description: A simplified decision problem where an agent repeatedly picks among several options with unknown random payoffs, trying to maximize total reward.

name: Off-policy learning
description: Learning about one policy, the target, from experience generated by a different policy, such as an older or more exploratory one.

name: Policy
description: The agent's rule for choosing an action in each situation, either fixed or given as probabilities over the possible actions.

name: Policy gradient
description: A family of methods that improve a policy directly by following the gradient of expected return with respect to the policy's parameters.

name: Proximal policy optimization
description: A policy gradient method that limits how far each update can move the policy by clipping the probability ratio between new and old policies.

name: Q-function
description: A function giving the expected discounted return from taking a specific action in a given state, then following a particular policy.

name: Q-learning
description: A temporal-difference method that learns the Q-function of the best possible policy from experience, even while exploring with a different policy.

name: REINFORCE
description: The basic policy gradient algorithm: play full episodes, then raise the log-probability of each action in proportion to the return that followed it.

name: Reinforcement learning
description: A kind of machine learning where an agent learns which actions to take by trial and error, guided by rewards from its environment.

name: Reward
description: A number an agent receives from its environment after acting, signaling how good the outcome was; the agent tries to maximize its total.

name: Temporal-difference learning
description: Learning value estimates step by step by nudging each toward the observed reward plus the discounted estimated value of the next state.

name: Trajectory
description: The sequence of states, actions, and rewards an agent experiences while interacting with its environment, such as one full game.

name: Trust region policy optimization
description: A policy gradient method that makes each update as large as safely possible by limiting the KL divergence between the old and new policies.

name: Value function
description: A function giving the expected discounted return an agent will collect starting from a given state while following a particular policy.

name: Ablation study
description: An experiment that removes or changes one part of a system at a time to measure how much that part contributes.

name: Accuracy
description: The fraction of examples a model gets exactly right, such as correct class predictions out of all predictions made.

name: Benchmark
description: A standard dataset and scoring procedure that many researchers use so different models can be compared fairly on the same task.

name: BLEU
description: A machine translation metric that scores output by how many of its short word sequences also appear in human reference translations.

name: CIFAR-10
description: A small benchmark of 60,000 tiny 32x32 color images in 10 classes, such as airplane, cat, and truck, widely used for quick experiments.

name: Data contamination
description: When benchmark test examples accidentally appear in a model's training data, inflating its scores because it may have memorized the answers.

name: Evaluation metric
description: A number that summarizes how well a model performs on a task, used to compare models and track progress.

name: Exact match
description: The percentage of predictions that match a correct reference answer character for character, usually after ignoring capitalization, punctuation, and articles.

name: F1 score
description: A single score combining precision and recall through their harmonic mean, so it is high only when both are high.

name: FLOPs
description: The number of basic arithmetic operations, such as additions and multiplications, a model needs, used to measure its computational cost.

name: Fréchet inception distance
description: A score comparing the mean and covariance of pretrained-classifier features for real and generated images; lower means more realistic, varied samples.

name: GLUE
description: A benchmark of nine English sentence-understanding tasks, such as sentiment analysis and natural language inference, scored together to compare models.

name: Human evaluation
description: Judging model outputs by asking people to rate or compare them, used when automatic metrics miss qualities like helpfulness or fluency.

name: ImageNet
description: A large image dataset whose standard version has about 1.2 million training photos in 1,000 categories, long the main image classification benchmark.
aliases: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge

name: ImageNet-21k
description: The full ImageNet dataset of roughly 14 million images in about 21,000 categories, often used to pretrain image models before fine-tuning.

name: Inference latency
description: The time a trained model takes to produce an output for one input, which matters for real-time and interactive applications.

name: JFT-300M
description: Google's internal dataset of about 300 million images with noisy, automatically generated labels, used to pretrain large image models like Vision Transformers.

name: Linear probing
description: Testing a pretrained model's learned features by freezing it and training only a simple linear classifier on top to solve a task.

name: LLM-as-a-judge
description: Using a strong large language model to grade or compare other models' outputs, as a cheaper, faster stand-in for human evaluation.

name: Mean average precision
description: A detection and retrieval metric that averages precision over all recall levels for each class or query, then averages across them.

name: MMLU
description: A benchmark of about 16,000 multiple-choice questions across 57 subjects, from math to law, testing a language model's knowledge and reasoning.

name: MNIST
description: A classic dataset of 70,000 small grayscale images of handwritten digits 0-9, often the first benchmark for image classification.

name: MS COCO
description: A large dataset of everyday scene photos labeled with object boxes, outlines, and captions, used to benchmark detection, segmentation, and captioning.

name: Perplexity
description: A language model metric equal to the exponential of average per-token cross-entropy; lower means the model is less surprised by real text.

name: Precision and recall
description: Precision is the share of predicted positives that are truly positive; recall is the share of actual positives the model finds.

name: ROUGE
description: A summarization metric that scores generated text by how many of the reference summary's words and word sequences it recovers.

name: SQuAD
description: The Stanford Question Answering Dataset, where models answer questions about Wikipedia paragraphs by pointing to the answer span in the text.

name: Top-k accuracy
description: The fraction of examples whose correct label appears among the model's k highest-scoring guesses, such as the top five.

name: VTAB
description: The Visual Task Adaptation Benchmark: 19 varied image tasks, each with only 1,000 training examples, testing how well pretrained models adapt.

name: Win rate
description: The fraction of head-to-head comparisons in which judges prefer one model's output over another's, often counting ties as half.

name: WMT
description: The Conference on Machine Translation, whose yearly competitions supply standard translation benchmarks like WMT 2014 English-German, usually scored with BLEU.
